subject: Order Form: insurance evidence sequencing and endorsement timeline
messages:
From: Claire Hudson <claire@acmeprocurement.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form insurance requirements and timing

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the updated order form. A couple of quick asks from our side to push the PO through with Finance:

- Can you confirm the timing for evidence delivery? We need a COI up front and an additional insured endorsement that names Acme Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries.
- Coverage minimums: commercial general liability $2M aggregate / $1M each occurrence; cyber liability $5M; auto combined single limit $1M. Please confirm these are met by Redwood's insurer.
- If endorsement issuance will take time, will an interim COI with a follow-up endorsement be acceptable? If so, what is the expected ETA?

Attached is the redlined order form (Acme_OrderForm_v3.pdf) — procurement would like to avoid exceptions but will escalate if timelines slip.

Appreciate a timeline and whether there are any carrier fees for the endorsement (we need to budget).

Best,
Claire Hudson
Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Order Form insurance requirements and timing

Hi Claire / Mateo,

Quick note from the broker side: we can issue an interim certificate of insurance (COI) within 48 hours once we have the signed order form and payment information. The additional insured endorsement is typically a separate endorsement process and carrier-dependent — standard timeline is 10-30 business days.

Carrier asks for the exact entity naming to be confirmed (Acme Holdings, Inc.; list of subsidiaries if you need them named explicitly) and whether Acme requires Primary/Non-Contributory language and Waiver of Subrogation. Those qualifiers can affect carrier approval time and sometimes incur a one-time endorsement charge (I will provide a quote).

I've attached a sample endorsement (endorsement_sample.pdf) and will pull an estimate for any endorsement fees for the carriers that underwrite Redwood. If procurement needs the COI immediately we can issue an interim COI showing limits; endorsement to follow.

Regards,
Julian Moss
Senior Account Executive
Wilson & Barr Insurance Brokers

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Julian Moss <julian.moss@wilsonbarr.com>, Claire Hudson <claire@acmeprocurement.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2025 10:34:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Order Form insurance requirements and timing

Kimberly / David — looping you in for legal/finance confirmation and to propose the playbook below for Acme.

Summary of status: broker can provide interim COI quickly, endorsement timeline ~10-30 business days, possible endorsement fee. Procurement wants the endorsement wording to name: "Acme Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries." Acme also requests coverage minima listed below.

Proposed mitigation / suggested contract language (for order form redline):
1) Interim COI delivered prior to effective date showing coverage limits and insurer name; final additional insured endorsement (or certificate and endorsement package) to be delivered within 45 calendar days of effective date.
2) Endorsement wording: "Acme Holdings, Inc., its subsidiaries and affiliates, as their interest may appear" — if Acme insists on explicit subsidiary listing, broker to provide required legal names.
3) Coverage qualifiers: Primary and Non-Contributory and Waiver of Subrogation requested; Redwood to provide if carrier agrees. If carrier cannot accommodate, Redwood to notify Acme within five business days and propose alternative (e.g., mutual waiver or extended reporting).
4) If carrier charges a one-time fee for issuance of endorsement, Redwood requests approval to pass-through the fee to Acme; procurement to confirm acceptance in writing.
5) Proof of policy retroactive date and policy number to be included on endorsement where applicable for cyber policies.

Action items:
- Kimberly: confirm acceptance of 45-day window and pass/fail on Primary/NNC/WS exposure.
- David: check if Finance is ok with potential pass-through of endorsement fee and confirm routing for invoice.
- Julian: please send carrier fee quote and an initial interim COI template once you have the signed order form.

If legal wants to shorten the window we can try, but in my experience 30-45 days is realistic for endorsements with large carriers. Happy to take a call with Acme procurement if they prefer.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

--

From: Claire Hudson <claire@acmeprocurement.com>

Thanks all — Acme can accept the proposed playbook with one clarifying note: 45 calendar days is acceptable provided the interim COI lists the carrier and limits and the endorsement is sent as soon as available; Acme Procurement will not pre-approve any fee pass-through greater than $500 without further approval.

Julian: please share the carrier fee quote (if any) and the interim COI as soon as available so we can cut the PO. We will sign the order form once we receive the interim COI and DocuSign link.

We'll expect the endorsement to reference the policy number and, if possible, include Primary/Non-Contributory language; if carrier denies those qualifiers, please provide a short note so we can route an exception.

Appreciate the responsiveness — Claire
